clue.text: Particular title picked up among the many books

indicators.note: something found among other words sits inside them, spanning the word boundaries
in a down clue, lifting something up reads it from the bottom, so the run of letters goes backwards

blocks.note: a run of letters straddling the three words

explanation.surface: Someone spots a particular title among a great pile of books.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters EMANYB lie across 'thE MANY Books'; read upwards they give BYNAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A byname is a secondary name or nickname, an individual title attached to one person.

clue.text: Harm in boasting symbol of ownership

indicators.note: one thing placed in another is enclosed by it, so the first word's letters go inside the second's

blocks.note: to mar is to harm or spoil

explanation.surface: Boasting can cause harm, the clue suggests, before tacking on a symbol of ownership.
explanation.walkthrough: Swank is showy bragging. A swan mark was the nick cut into a swan's bill to show who owned the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Swans on the Thames were marked on the beak to identify their owners, so the mark proved possession.

clue.text: Member's decoration granted power at first

indicators.note: placed at first means this element comes ahead of the other at the start

blocks.note: arm as in strength or authority, the long arm of the law

explanation.surface: A club member is awarded a decoration and given power to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' looks like a club member but is a limb, the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: An armlet is a band or bracelet worn round the arm, an ornament for that limb.

clue.text: Church dissenter leading curtailed Mass - movement co-ordinator?

indicators.note: leading means coming in front, so these elements precede what follows
curtailed means having its tail cut off, losing its final letter

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church dissenter leads a shortened Mass while some protest movement is co-ordinated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' with its capital looks liturgical, but it is a lump, docked to LUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The cerebellum is the part of the brain that co-ordinates muscular movement and balance; the question mark flags the descriptive definition.

clue.text: Form or class? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means a little short of complete, so the word loses its end

blocks.note: a caste is a social class

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a form at school is quite the same thing as a class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form or class' looks like two synonyms for a school group; only the first is a definition, the mould sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast is a mould or shape, as in the cast of someone's features, so it means form.

clue.text: Jotted down notes, being calm

explanation.surface: Someone takes notes while staying cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' suggests memos; they are musical notes, written down by a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: To compose is to write music, and composed also describes a person who is collected and serene.

clue.text: Difficult situation - not quite additional example of idiocy

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: an ass is a fool, a walking instance of idiocy

explanation.surface: A tricky spot arises from yet another instance of stupidity.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is literally a bog, and figuratively a mess one cannot get out of.

clue.text: See 21
Caught male leaving disturbed cemetery, carrying wide feature of cemeteries?

indicators.note: the two letters leaving the word means they are taken out of it
something disturbed is thrown out of order, so its letters are jumbled
carrying something means holding it within, so one letter goes inside the rest

blocks.note: c is the cricket abbreviation for caught
w is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A man departs a disturbed graveyard while a cricketing scene drifts in with caught and wide.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip C and M from CEMETERY, jumble the remaining EETERY and hold W inside. Caught and wide are cricket scorebook abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Yews are traditionally planted in English churchyards, so the tree is a typical sight among graves.

clue.text: Salamander all too unsettled around centre of Texas

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter alone
unsettled letters are disturbed from their order and rearranged
the jumbled letters go around the other piece, enclosing it

explanation.surface: A salamander is all too restless somewhere in the heart of Texas.
explanation.definitionFit: The axolotl is a Mexican salamander that keeps its larval gills into adulthood.

clue.text: Cancelling tunnel man dug up

indicators.note: ground that is dug up is churned over, so the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A tunnelling project is called off because the workman's excavation is being dug up.
explanation.definitionFit: An annulment is the act of declaring something void, the noun for cancelling it.

clue.text: Backed suggestion about the French hairstyle

indicators.note: backed means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse
about means surrounding, so this word goes around the next

blocks.note: a tip is a hint or suggestion
la is French for the, feminine

explanation.surface: Someone supports a proposal about the French way of doing hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' reads as supported, but it turns the tip round to PIT, which then wraps LA.
explanation.definitionFit: A plait is hair divided into strands and woven together, a braid.

clue.text: Precision in disposal of next cases

indicators.note: disposal can mean arrangement, as in troops at one's disposal, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: Care is needed in getting rid of the next cases on a docket.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactness is the quality of being accurate and correct, a synonym of precision.

clue.text: Helping it to rise, very into redefined purpose

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading from the bottom up, backwards
redefined means given a new form, so the letters are rearranged
into means placed inside, so these letters are set within the others

blocks.note: v is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Someone helping a cause lifts it, putting real energy into a reworked purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes the abbreviation for very along with the seven letters of the word purpose; the upturned pronoun then slots in near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Supportive means giving help and encouragement, so it fits helping as an adjective.

clue.text: Rice dish - mum's invested in outfit almost completely

indicators.note: something invested in another is clothed by it, placed inside
almost completely means everything but the last bit, so a final letter goes

blocks.note: mum means silent, and sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: Mother has money tied up in a nearly finished outfit while dinner is rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not mother but the word for keeping quiet, as in 'mum's the word'; SH goes inside SUI(T).
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is the Japanese dish of vinegared rice topped or rolled with fish.

clue.text: Dessert successfully brought to couch potato after work in kitchen

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the remaining pieces follow this one

blocks.note: a pudding is slang for a fat, sluggish person

explanation.surface: A dessert is triumphantly brought to a lazy television watcher by the cook.
explanation.walkthrough: Pudding is British slang for a podgy, idle person, so it stands for the couch potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Bakewell pudding is a Derbyshire dessert of pastry with jam and an egg-almond filling.

clue.text: Gathering indication of flowering, including Northern heather

indicators.note: including means holding inside, so the next letter goes within

blocks.note: a bud signals a flower to come

explanation.surface: A gardener gathers signs of blossom on northern heather.
explanation.definitionFit: Bundling is tying things together in a bundle, a way of collecting them up.

clue.text: Conflict over medic getting award for contribution to operating theatre?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so this piece comes first

blocks.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A war surgeon is honoured for services in the operating theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operating theatre' suggests surgery; read it as a working stage theatre, which has a costume department.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre's wardrobe department supplies the costumes, so it contributes to a running playhouse.

clue.text: Popular group to include European starlets

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so a letter goes inside

blocks.note: a genus is a group in classification

explanation.surface: A popular band takes on European starlets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popular group' looks like a pop band but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingenue is an innocent young actress or the role she plays, much like a starlet.

clue.text: North America, mostly dreadful, the worst place

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: NA is short for North America

explanation.surface: A grumble that North America is largely awful and the worst place to be.
explanation.definitionFit: A nadir is the lowest point, so it fits the worst place figuratively.

clue.text: Busy person duly disheartened, old chap's upset

indicators.note: losing the heart leaves only the outer letters of the word
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the outer letters, with the middle removed

explanation.surface: An energetic person is suitably downcast because an old friend is upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a generator, and by extension a tirelessly energetic person.

clue.text: Line in second working socket possibly moving suddenly

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a machine that is on is working
a socket is one kind of light fitting, hence possibly

explanation.surface: An electrician jumps as a line in a working socket suddenly moves.
explanation.walkthrough: MO + ON + LIGHT F(L)ITTING. A moonlight flit is leaving home at night, usually to dodge rent.
explanation.definitionFit: A moonlight flitting is a hasty secret house move by night, often to escape debts, so it means relocating abruptly.

clue.text: Uniform but disordered?

blocks.note: first meaning: distinctive dress of servants or a company
second meaning: suffering a liver disorder, hence bilious and irritable

explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays uniform against disordered as opposites; the second sense is the adjective meaning liverish, a liver disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery is the dress worn by servants or guild members, and as an adjective it means bilious or irritable.

clue.text: Period in which British will exhibit sound tone

indicators.note: in which means inside the first thing, so the next piece goes within it

explanation.surface: A historical period in which Britain shows a sound tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like healthy, as in sound judgement; here it is the acoustic sense, part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbre is the characteristic quality or colour of a sound, distinct from its pitch.

clue.text: Looking up naturally allows review, initially of celestial object

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of each word counts

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of five words

explanation.surface: Gazing skywards naturally lets one survey a heavenly body.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunar means relating to the moon, the most familiar celestial body in the sky.

clue.text: Neutralising element redeployed on Vietnam

indicators.note: troops redeployed are moved into new positions, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A military unit is moved to Vietnam to neutralise the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: Antivenom is the serum that counteracts snake or insect poison, cancelling out its effect.

clue.text: A deviation, swinging round in different direction

indicators.note: swinging round means turning to face the other way, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: yaw is a ship or aircraft's deviation from its course

explanation.surface: A vessel veers off course, swinging round to head elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Away means off in another direction, as in turning away from something.

clue.text: I'm a Nationalist repelled by a lot of prejudice in African country

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back, so its letters run backwards
a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A nationalist complains of being rebuffed by widespread prejudice in an African state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' simply joins the two pieces: reversed IMAN, then BIA(S).
explanation.definitionFit: Namibia is a country in south-west Africa, formerly South West Africa.

clue.text: Painter's change in direction after capturing the writer following completion of chapter

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it inside, so those letters go within
following means coming after, so this piece is placed later

blocks.note: to veer is to change direction
the writer of the clue refers to the setter, me

explanation.surface: An artist changes course after the author finishes a chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: VE(R+ME)ER. 'The writer' is the setter speaking of themselves as ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Vermeer was the seventeenth-century Dutch artist of Girl with a Pearl Earring.
